summary: Innovation is a fast-paced tableau-builder where you race through ages of technology, splaying cards to reveal icons and chaining dogpile combos that can swing the game in a single turn. It's brutally interactive despite having no board or dice — you're constantly reading opponents' tableaus and timing when to demand, share, or rush an achievement before they do.
praised: Incredible depth and replayability from a small deck of cards
Elegant, tightly integrated rules where every card's effect ties into its theme
Explosive, satisfying combo turns once you see the engine click
Fast to play and easy to reset for another game
criticised: Steep learning curve and dense rules text on cards makes early games confusing
Can feel swingy or 'solved' by a single big combo that ends the game abruptly
Kingmaking and analysis paralysis in multiplayer as players parse others' boards
Iconography and card interactions are hard to teach to new players

interaction.kind: sharing/demanding effects and tableau disruption (take that)

scoring.why: The game is won by claiming achievements (via score thresholds or special criteria), not by tallying broad point sources, so a single well-timed combo or dogma chain usually decides the winner.
